      <description><p>The returning James Maddison scored a beauty, with Omar Marmoush and Ben Davies also on target as Spurs won in the league for the first time this season</p><p><strong>Where is the game? </strong>Spurs will look to dominate possession, with Gray and Tonali dictating play, so Maddison, Kudus and Marmoush can buzz about behind Solanke.       <title>Davies ensures Spurs off the bottom after first win of season against Coventry</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/19/tottenham-coventry-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>Tottenham are level with Beyoncé at last. Progress is represented in Roberto De Zerbi’s side earning only their sixth home win in the Premier League since November 2024. Cynics will point out that this spectacular stadium has hosted as many Beyoncé gigs during that time, but Spurs are finally singing a happier tune after dragging themselves out of the bottom three thanks to a messy but gritty 3-1 win over Coventry.</p><p>It was not especially convincing. Coventry raged at the second Spurs goal, delivered when Omar Marmoush responded to Jack Rudoni’s equaliser for the visitors with a vicious effort in the 59th minute. Relief poured out of Marmoush after his first goal since joining on loan from Manchester City, but should it have stood? The Egyptian forward, who otherwise had a quiet game, was fortunate not to be penalised for an elbow on Milan van Ewijk.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/19/tottenham-coventry-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Florian Wirtz takes on more responsibility in Liverpool’s attack while Pierre Sage is under pressure at Crystal Palace</p><p>Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s physicality overpowering Bryan Mbeumo in Manchester United’s area at a corner grabbed him a fifth goal in 10 outings for Leeds: a pretty respectable ratio. “I just tried to cause a ruckus,” said Leeds’ No 9. “I make it difficult for the defender. I read the flight of the ball and was quickest to react. I feel really comfortable [here]. I feel the support from the club and the fans and it is a great feeling stepping on to the pitch, particularly at Elland Road.” Of the contenders to be understudy to Harry Kane as England’s centre-forward, Calvert-Lewin may be the lead act – if he can stay injury-free, which has been a difficulty throughout his career. <strong>Jamie Jackson</strong></p><p>Match report: <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/18/leeds-manchester-united-premier-league-match-report">Leeds 1-1 Manchester United</a></p><p>Match report: <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/17/brentford-liverpool-premier-league-match-report">Brentford 1-2 Liverpool</a></p><p>Match report: <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/17/manchester-city-ipswich-premier-league-match-report">Manchester City 3-2 Ipswich</a></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/19/premier-league-10-talking-points-from-the-weekends-action">Continue reading...</a></description>
